findings.summary: Custom operation declarations are necessary static upstream wire selection, not performance tuning. Source-backed explanations are in the gateway why files.
Higress OpenAI-to-Cohere and Messages-to-Cohere return invalid responses. Both supported cells stay enabled.
LiteLLM Rust Chat-to-Bedrock rejects the standard max_tokens parameter with 501. Its implemented Converse adapter is configured and declared supported; no request workaround.

Every manifest now declares the full 6x6 support grid. Helicone correct native paths verify five pairs; Plano verifies seven with normal provider identities; LiteLLM Python declares 26 supported pairs including the omitted native passthrough paths, with one real invalid-response failure retained.

Removed the new global LiteLLM Python Messages-to-Chat routing override. Its per-model setting already selects the correct Chat upstream; changing the global internal bridge concealed an empty-response failure. All 26 supported cells stay enabled, including that failure.

Common classifier now retains a supported-cell 404/501 as Failed, preserves raw response evidence, and keeps rig-health and identical retry rules. Unsupported declarations still skip probes. No gateway identity enters the engine rule.

Released standalone LiteLLM Rust explicitly rejects OpenAI Chat streaming (native OpenAI and Anthropic upstream adapters) with 501. Native Messages streaming works. Do not substitute a different gateway/runtime or change workloads to hide this.

Build one immutable ARM64 engine/mock bundle from the corrected committed source via the existing verify-engine CI job. Full CI and artifact verification occur during the requested later release. Obtain instrument-matched control calibration; do not reuse the older binary baseline.
